title: Peer networking support: embedded members-only relay, signed relay advertisements and gossip, network diagnostics
description: Security-first native networking in fe-sync on iroh 1.3, delivered for self-hosters and verse operators. Six requirements: (FR-1) an embedded iroh-relay server in fe-relay, opt-in at build time and at runtime, off by default, TLS via ACME or an operator-supplied cert, and refusing to start when misconfigured; (FR-2) a relay-capable desktop mode gated by a net_report reachability self-test plus an AutoNAT-style HTTPS dial-back with SSRF-pinned probing; (FR-3) members-only relay access control: an AccessControl gate admitting only explicit Viewer+ declared verse members (never open_to_all), per-endpoint and global connection caps, client_rx bandwidth caps, eviction on revocation via Clients::disconnect, and rate-limited abuse logging; (FR-4) hardening of the S-RELAY-ADVERTISE seam from relay_operability_20261031: inner ed25519 signature, role check at read time, TTL, bounded set, health checks, DialOnly-by-default adoption (hazard B: the iroh home relay is endpoint-global), a refcounted fallback that never removes configured relays, isolation of the operator token, and a peer-address relay-URL filter; (FR-5) per-message gossip signing that closes residual S-1, with replay defence and a compat/require mixed-version rollout using a per-author latch; (FR-6) truthful direct/relayed diagnostics in the GUI, API and MCP, read-only, scope-confined and IP-redacted. Four embedded Fable review gates (F0-F3) each record a verdict file; any FAIL blocks the next wave.
origin: user directive 2026-10-31: networking support feature, secure, Fable-reviewed (from NAT/relay research session findings)
alignment: Open-core public side (conductor/open-core.md): anything a self-hoster needs to run, verify or extend FractalEngine. Consumes and hardens seam S-RELAY-ADVERTISE, which relay_operability_20261031 FR-7 owns. Closes SECURITY.md's gossip-attribution limitation (S-1, fe-sync/src/AGENTS.md §transport-admission-control item 2) and the §write-policy requirement that networked operations be signed. Plugins stay network-less (fe-plugin capability network_scope/external_http are unenforced; the WIT is aspirational), so networking remains native fe-sync work.

notes: 2026-10-31: track drafted (docs only). Every iroh claim is cited against registry sources: iroh-1.3.0, iroh-relay-1.3.0, iroh-gossip-0.101.0, iroh-docs-0.101.0.
Verified findings from the research session, folded in:
(a) Hole-punching is automatic. NAT candidates travel as QUIC frames inside the E2E connection (remote_state.rs:534,947). Portmapping defaults to Enabled (portmapper.rs:20-38).

(b) insert_relay/remove_relay exist (endpoint.rs:1000,1014). The relay map supplies only auth_token and home candidacy (actor.rs:1342-1346). iroh dials any relay URL found in a remote's address even if it is not in the map (actor.rs:1279-1322). This motivates both the peer-address filter and DialOnly adoption.
(c) There is a single home relay, chosen from net_report preferred_relay (actor.rs:1235-1265). Hazard B: a members-only relay that becomes the home relay cuts off peers from other verses.
(d) The relay AccessControl hook runs after a handshake that proves the EndpointId (http_server.rs:866-878). accept_conn_limit/burst are unimplemented (server.rs:486-500).

(e) CORRECTION to the coordinator brief item A3: an EMBEDDED relay can evict live sessions via Server::relay_service() (server.rs:949) → RelayService::clients() (http_server.rs:953) → Clients::disconnect (clients.rs:181). Only the standalone binary lacks eviction.
(f) iroh-docs rows are SignedEntry-authenticated (sync.rs:698-702). Gossip Message is unsigned (api.rs:362-371). The claim-based residual is therefore gossip-only.
(g) net_report is behind the unstable-net-report feature (endpoint.rs:1456). All UDP probes are insufficient for relay serving, which needs inbound TCP/HTTPS; hence the dial-back requirement.
(h) iroh test-utils provides run_relay_server_with_access (test_utils.rs:51), and Builder::clear_ip_transports (endpoint.rs:510) builds relay-only endpoints. The e2e flows need no docker.
(i) VerseFabric::access_snapshot folds in open_to_all (docs_engine.rs:44-53). Reusing it for the relay gate would create an open relay, so a new relay_admission_snapshot is required.

Spec §8 lists 8 changes required in relay_operability_20261031: OD-6 default → DialOnly; a versioned __relays row; read-time admission with demotion re-evaluation; cross-verse refcount and never removing Configured URLs; no RelayAccessToken on advertised relays; correcting the FR-7 risk text (the residual is gossip-only); one shared URL validator; a cross-reference to this track as the embedded-server phase. All eight were applied to that track at Gate F0.

2026-10-31: Fable F0 design review — PASS-WITH-FIXES. 16 findings (4 high, 7 medium, 5 low), all fixed in place: OD-4 drops the __peers intersection (bootstrap deadlock for relay-only newcomers); revocation made convergent (on_connect precedes Clients::register, so a one-shot generation check could miss); replay LRU made per-(verse, author); dial-back request names one prober and probers are servers by default; every resolved address must be public; OD-3 verifier contract written (live pin set by exact ServerName, WebPKI delegation incl. signature methods, no pins for Configured/Default hosts); portmapped-address-in-watch_addr confirmed; AC-9 decided as the documented warning path; OD-13 coverage auto-home added (user decision pending); planner gains a Default tier distinct from Configured. tripwires: relay gate never consults default_access/open_to_all — explicit Viewer+ statements only, never gated on a __peers row (F0: the intersection deadlocked relay-only newcomers)
revocation is convergent: the gate keeps its own endpoint_id → connection_id table and retries Clients::disconnect until on_disconnect fires for every entry (on_connect runs before register)
certificate pins (OD-3 phase) are keyed by exact ServerName and never installed for a Configured or Default relay host; the verifier always delegates signature checks to WebPKI
Default (n0) relays are demoted only while a coverage-eligible advertised relay is connected as home, and re-inserted on any failure signal; explicit Configured relays are never demoted
embedded relay: never AllowAll, never plaintext outside #[cfg(test)], absent unless cargo feature built AND FE_RELAY_SERVE=1; refuse to start without cert mode or served verses
advertised relays never carry RelayAccessToken (insert with auth_token: None); advertisement processing never removes a Configured relay URL
adoption state (DialOnly/HomeEligible/Ignore, pins, denies) is local-only, never replicated
a frame bearing the FEG1 signed magic that fails verification is dropped, never re-parsed as legacy
dial-back prober connects only to resolved public unicast IPs, fixed path, no redirects
client IPs never logged and diagnostics redact IPs by default
any Fable gate FAIL blocks the next wave; F1-F3 fix their own findings
